assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, active GLP-1(7-36) amide) led to therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Original, clear and of very large clinical and societal reach, with a well-defined chain from physiology to drug.
assessment.attribution: Holst and Drucker made central physiological and mechanistic contributions; Mojsov's identification of the active peptide form is a decisive and sometimes disputed contribution. Knudsen carried the pharmaceutical development, so a trio is a judgement call between discovery and development credit; Habener is not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy confirmed in many large independent trials over more than a decade; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation between Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen is unresolved and Habener's role cannot be credited from this list.
Priority disputes around Mojsov's contribution are from my general knowledge and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light, enabling a generation of circuit studies. A true enabling method with broad adoption; clinical use (vision restoration) is early but the experimental impact is established.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth; Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted approach) make a six-name field. A three-person limit forces exclusion of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, which is a real weakness.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than 15 years of independent replication and ubiquitous use; timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among six credited names is contested and cannot fit three laureates cleanly.
Whether the committee prefers the molecular discovery or the neuronal application is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. Strong originality and lasting impact on cancer immunology and cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June are linked to the design and clinical translation of CAR constructs; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early CAR clinical work. Eshhar, Kuwana and others are not on the supplied list and the original CAR concept credit is not captured.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term follow-up support the clinical effect; solid-tumour and toxicity limits remain but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Missing early-concept contributors (not in the credited names) complicate a fair prize configuration.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR defined a central nutrient-sensing regulator of cell growth with relevance to metabolism, ageing, cancer and immunosuppression. Conceptually foundational and widely confirmed.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast, Schreiber's rapamycin-target chemical biology led to FKBP12-rapamycin work, and Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR components. Brown and Heitman also contributed, so allocation is uncertain; Hall is the clearest core.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of replication and clinical drugs (rapalogs); timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Priority among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and others not in the list is a matter of judgement.
Clinical impact of rapalogs is narrower than the biological significance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signaling and links proteostasis to disease. Elegant, original and foundational mechanistic discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently dissected the Ire1/Hac1 signaling pathway in yeast; the two-person configuration is coherent. Other contributors (e.g. Ron, Harding) are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Well-confirmed across species for more than two decades; timely and mature, though therapeutic translation is still developing.
uncertainties: Mammalian UPR branches and other contributors lie outside the credited names.
Translational impact is less established than the basic-science impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, which changed the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy and validated antisense oligonucleotides as a platform. Excellent combination of mechanism and clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's splicing mechanism work and Bennett's oligonucleotide chemistry and development form a plausible pair. Other contributors (Gene Hua, Hua and Singh, Monani) are not on the list, and the roles of the academic and industry teams may need separating.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world data; the broader antisense platform's maturity is still growing, so recognition is slightly early but defensible.
uncertainties: Credit partitioning between splicing-mechanism and drug-chemistry contributions is not fully resolved.
Longer-term durability and treatment-timing effects are still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis reshaped genomics and clinical diagnostics and underlies much of single-cell and spatial biology. Transformational as an enabling technology.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman led the Solexa chemistry and Mayer contributed to the parallel colony approach; however, technology credit is tangled with other platforms and industry teams. I note that my own field depends on this technology, and I judge the credit question on its own merits.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and ubiquitous; recognition is arguably late, though it may be seen as a chemistry or technology rather than physiology or medicine prize.
uncertainties: Whether the prize scope fits technology development is uncertain.
Credit competes with other sequencing platform inventors outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Positional cloning of leptin revealed an adipose-derived hormone controlling appetite and body weight and opened the field of energy-balance endocrinology. Clear, original and highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Friedman led the cloning of the ob gene and the hormone's characterisation. Douglas Coleman's parabiosis work was essential but he is deceased and not in the credited names, and a single laureate is a thin configuration; Leibel and Zhang are also associated with the work.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, including leptin-replacement therapy in lipodystrophy and congenital deficiency; the broader obesity impact is mixed, and recognition is long established.
uncertainties: Whether a single living laureate is a fair configuration given Coleman and collaborators.
Therapeutic impact is narrower than the physiological significance.
